h: First Time on the Ice? Read This
p: Nobody glides out like a pro on their first go, so don't put that pressure on yourself. The trick is to bend your knees a little, keep your weight slightly forward and take small, shuffly steps rather than trying to walk normally. Look ahead, not down at your feet. And if you feel yourself going, crouch and let yourself drop sideways rather than flapping backwards. It's far less painful and far more dignified.

Getting back up is a skill in itself. Roll onto your knees, put one foot flat on the ice, then the other, and push up slowly with your hands on your knees. Practise it once early on and you'll feel a lot braver for the rest of the session.

Hire skates should be snug but not crushing, with laces pulled tight around the ankle for support. Loose skates are the number one cause of wobbly ankles, so it's worth taking an extra minute at the bench to get them right. Thin, long socks work better than chunky bed socks, and gloves are a must for when you inevitably meet the ice.

Once you're done, Altrincham is a great little town to explore. The Market House is a buzzing spot for food and drink, with plenty of independent traders under one roof, and Dunham Massey, the National Trust estate with its deer park, is just outside town for a lovely walk on a dry day. Skate in the morning, stroll in the afternoon, and you've got a proper Cheshire day out.
